THE BAND WAS THE ONE PROMISING SHAPE AND IT FAILS FOR A CLEAN REASON. All nine subjects sit ABOVE the 93 knee (raw 94.11 to 100.94) and both pins sit BELOW it (Gervin 89.90, Kareem 87.46), so a flatter stretch above the knee would have cut the subjects and left the pins untouched to the byte. But every post-84 card he calls fine is in the SAME stretch — Dantley '84 raw 99.47, King '84 94.64, Bird '86 100.34, Malone '90 97.19 — and a band is a function of the raw score alone, so it cannot tell 1981 from 1984. WHY THERE IS NO PRE-84 EDGE TO CUT ON, and this is the whole round in one table. recal_196's era share is a function of ONE quantity, the league's own mean 3pt rating that season, and it is FLAT across exactly the years the ruling divides: 1980 14.79, 1981 13.53, 1982 14.65, 1983 13.64, 1984 14.01, then 1985 15.59, 1986 16.57, 1987 18.83. The 3pt line was adopted gradually and 1984 shot it no more than 1981 did. So the era shares read 0.943 / 1.000 / 0.950 / 0.995 / 0.979 / 0.907 / 0.863 — 1984 sits BETWEEN 1980 and 1983, ABOVE 1985. Any monotone reshaping of the ramp that cuts 1981 cuts 1984 at least as hard. 294 (foot, full, power) settings were measured: the best that holds every pin and every post-84 card reaches ZERO of the nine.

THE TWO-CARD PROOF, which needs no sweep at all. Adrian Dantley '81 (asked 92, so he must read 95 or below) and Adrian Dantley '84 (called fine at 97, so he must read 96 or above). Today they both print 97 and their o_scores are 107.617 and 106.959 — '81 is 0.658 HIGHER. The round would have to cross them and then open 1.75 of o_score on top, and the ONLY things the file can read between them are: z 99/87/12 against 93/92/14, playvol 48 against 50, volume 94 against 93, efficiency 99 against 95, era 1.000 against 0.979. '81 leads on best zone and on efficiency, so cutting him harder means paying LESS for a better weapon and better shooting, which is precisely the inversion recal_210 outlawed and which this file now prints a monotonicity count for on every run. '81 trails on second zone, third zone and playvol, so cutting him harder on any of those takes Kareem Abdul-Jabbar '80 (second zone 64, the lowest of the whole class, and at the floor of his pin) down first and hardest.

THE SAME COLLISION, THREE MORE TIMES, on the one axis the dispatch flagged: playvol. Dantley '82 and Kareem '80 are BOTH playvol 49 — one must lose 2.421 of o_score, the other may lose 1.027. Dantley '80 and Bernard King '84 are BOTH playvol 39 — one must lose 3.029, the other may lose 2.303. Erving '80 needs 39.0% of his clearance leg at playvol 64 while Bird '83 admits 38.3% of his at playvol 68, so even the ordering is backwards. A creation fade is the right instinct — Westphal (74) against Gervin (34) is exactly the pair it separates — but the class is not sorted by creation.

THE WIDE SEARCH, and it is the strongest statement in the round. Not just the era term: ANY new subtractive term gated on the same pre-1997 inferred class (so 1997+ stays byte-identical), of the form -K x ramp(x, lo, hi), over 26 attributes x every ramp on that attribute's own values x 8 depths x both directions. Clean settings — zero anchor failures AND zero post-84 cards moving more than a point — number SEVEN, they all reach at most TWO of the nine, and every one of them is a gate on era in (0.995, 1.000], which is a selector for the 1981 season and nothing else. A one-season gate is a per-player override wearing a ramp, and doctrine 1 forbids it. The same search run on recal_196's own two legs (fade the coefficient, or fade the clearance leg alone) gives three clean settings, each reaching ONE subject, each a selector for a single card: a clearance gate at 80-84 catches Dantley '80 alone, a coefficient gate at 0.125-0.135 catches the 1981/1983 full-load cards alone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE ABOUT THE CLASS, for the next round. recal_196's term is the largest single payment on the 1980-83 board — 7.2 to 8.0 of o_score on the nine subjects, against o_scores of 101 to 109 — and it is paid almost entirely on the CLEARANCE leg (6.4 to 6.8) rather than recal_210's balance (0.6 to 1.3). The cards he calls fine from 1985 on divide in two: the no-third-zone scorers (Dantley '84-'86, King '84/'85, Malone '89-'93) collect the SAME clearance leg and fall with the subjects, while the three-zone cards (Bird '85-'88) collect almost pure balance and do not. So the only clean line the term draws is 'has a third zone' against 'has not' — and Dantley '81 and Dantley '84 are on the same side of it.

The release it takes to land all nine is FIVE pins — Gervin '80, Kareem '80, Bird '83, Jordan '87, Hakeem '94 — plus the post-84 +-1 on 214 cards from 1984-96, every one of which he has just called fine.
